analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, lines 1536-1982. They sit in older release sections (v0.9.12 to v0.9.18 and preparatory notes) and are unchanged context. The patch's changed head range is lines 11-176, which these units do not display. The units hold documentation only, with no executable code, so they add no new attack surface, regression or invalidated assumption.

The prose touches several threat-model areas, but each entry describes behavior that was already shipped or pre-existing. None of it is a new change in this PR:
- SSD prefix-cache write-endurance budget, HMAC-keyed names, TTL and per-account cacheSalt scoping (T-041/SEC-035). The changelog states the cache scope and encryption are unchanged.
- Frozen legacy MDM and App Attest authorization (T-052/T-053/T-054). The changelog describes these as fail-closed.
- Account erasure and soft-delete.
- Coordinator log PII removal.
- Provider-bound body scrubbing of the `user`, `metadata`, `safety_identifier` and `prompt_cache_key` fields. This matches the threat model's statement that caller cache keys do not participate in scoping.

The v0.10.5 section, which carries the new behavior, includes the MLX pin bump, the `darkbloom sandbox` installer (TB-013/T-061) and the add-on hold socket (TB-012). It falls outside the supplied units. Any security conclusion about those rollout notes needs the patch ranges at head lines 11-176 and the corresponding source diffs. The excerpts I saw give no evidence of a regression, and I cannot confirm the claims from them. I recommend that the integration pass review the v0.10.5 changelog hunk against the actual code changes (pin bumps, sandbox installer integrity checks, hold socket).
